clue.text: Son with access details securing English liquor

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: the username and password that let you into a system
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A son's password details guard an English drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Access details are what you type to get into an account; the son's letter stands in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloe gin is a liqueur made by steeping sloe berries in gin, so it is a liquor.

clue.text: Magnificent vehicle turning green

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: A splendid car changes colour to green.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means of supreme excellence or beauty, so it is a synonym of magnificent.

clue.text: Pole peeled the setter's fruit

indicators.note: peeling strips away the outer layer, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
the setter is I, and the setter's has stands for I have, I'VE

explanation.surface: A Polish person stripped the skin from the fruit belonging to the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's reads as possessive, but it is I + 's = I'VE (I have).
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is the small oily stone fruit of the olive tree.

clue.text: Ex-PM happy with weight

parts.note: glad means happy
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is pleased about their weight.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone served four times as British prime minister in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Sound of hooter one's blocked

indicators.note: a blocked passage has something stuck inside it

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The honk of a hooter is muffled because it is stuffed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is': the nose is blocked by one. Sound of hooter tempts a reading as a horn's honk.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is any sound, especially a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: Really great editor provides something to kip on

parts.note: SO (really) plus FAB (great)
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A wonderful editor offers a place to nap.
explanation.walkthrough: To kip is British slang for to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa bed folds out into a bed, a piece of furniture for sleeping on.

clue.text: Most harsh putting second fool briefly on trial

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to fool someone is to trick them
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A judge is at their sternest when briefly deceiving the second defendant on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places TEST after the rest in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictest is the superlative of strict, meaning the most severe or harsh.

clue.text: Force working to apprehend the Spanish crook

indicators.note: apprehending someone means seizing and holding them, so one piece takes in another

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force
a machine that is on is working
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Police officers on duty arrest a Spanish criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone convicted of a serious crime, so a crook.

clue.text: Colouring option Lee rubs in vigorously

indicators.note: doing something vigorously churns it up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A hairdresser named Lee massages a hair dye in firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue rinse is a tint used on grey hair, so it is one choice of hair colouring.

clue.text: Move quickly on river filming equipment

parts.note: to dash is to rush
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone hurries along a river carrying a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'on' puts the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashcam is a small camera mounted on a car's dashboard that records the road.

clue.text: Dire bar GI renovated for officer

indicators.note: renovated things are rebuilt and remodelled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A shabby bar frequented by an American soldier is done up for an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer commanding a brigade.

clue.text: Oafs in great numbers bored by university

indicators.note: something bored by another has that other drilled into its middle

parts.note: lots means large numbers
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Crowds of oafs are found at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Louts and oafs are both crude, clumsy and boorish people.

clue.text: Some deride a sceptic's views

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the answer is a stretch of the letters that follow

parts.note: the run of letters straddling deride, a and sceptic

explanation.surface: Some people mock a doubter's opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across derIDE A Sceptic; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are opinions or notions, which is what views are.

clue.text: Odd way of talking initially ignored in Morecambe?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a famous British comedian, so Morecambe? clues his first name

indicators.note: ignoring something at the start means dropping its opening letter

parts.note: an accent is a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A peculiar manner of speech heard in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but here it stands for Eric Morecambe of the comedy duo Morecambe and Wise; the question mark flags the trick. ACCENT loses its A and sits inside ERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eccentric is unconventional and strange, which is what odd means.

clue.text: Spying wild ponies inside of cages

indicators.note: wild means unruly and out of order, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the inside of a word is all of it but its outer letters

parts.note: cages without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone spots untamed horses in pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Espionage is the practice of spying, gathering secret information.

clue.text: Softly shifting arboreal white-furred animal

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for softly

indicators.note: shifting things move about, so these letters change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A white-furred creature quietly moves through the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Arboreal means tree-dwelling, which a polar bear never is.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar bear is the large Arctic bear with thick white fur.

clue.text: A knight tipped dram over the French philosopher

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something tipped over is upended, so in a down answer the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
a tot is a small measure of spirits
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A knight knocked back a whisky ahead of a French thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'over' puts TOT above LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato and tutor of Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Note car close to prom

parts.note: the Mini is a classic small British car

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of prom

explanation.surface: Someone notes a car parked near the seafront promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note, the half note worth two crotchets.

clue.text: Spread of fish trousered by one serving aboard ship

indicators.note: to trouser something is to pocket it, so one piece is tucked inside the other

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving on a ship
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A sailor pockets a range of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Spread of fish reads as an array of seafood; spread is the definition and of is a link. To trouser is British slang for to pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that you spread on bread.

clue.text: Female eating tips of little carrots sweetly

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a doe is a female deer or rabbit

indicators.note: the tips of words are their first letters

parts.note: the opening letters of little and carrots

explanation.surface: A female rabbit nibbles baby carrots in a dainty way.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolce is the musical direction meaning to play sweetly and softly.

clue.text: Act to retain 75 per cent of mail removed from office

indicators.note: retaining something means keeping hold of it inside

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: three quarters of a four-letter word keeps three letters and drops the last

parts.note: post is mail

explanation.surface: A law is passed to keep most of the mail, and a minister is ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: Deposed describes a ruler or official forced out of a position of power.

clue.text: Cross group of followers east of Bury

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a sect is a body of followers of a creed

explanation.surface: A band of devotees settles to the east of Bury, a town near Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'east of' puts SECT to the right of the word for Bury. Bury looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that intersect cross each other, so the verb cross is a synonym.

clue.text: Enthusiast up regularly in Shiraz country

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the word reads from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a nut is a fanatic, as in a fitness nut

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the odd-placed letters of in Shiraz

explanation.surface: A wine buff raves about Shiraz from a certain country.
explanation.walkthrough: Shiraz is a wine and an Iranian city, but here it just lends letters along with in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a country in North Africa.

clue.text: Scrounging soldier put in charge

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
to sit something somewhere is to put it there
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A soldier is given command of a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasitic person lives off others, which is exactly what scrounging describes.

clue.text: Cancel last parts of dubious Tantric massage

indicators.note: the last parts of words are their final letters

parts.note: the final letters of dubious and Tantric
a rub is a massage

explanation.surface: Someone calls off the end of a questionable spa treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: To scrub a plan is informal for to cancel it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrub is an informal verb for calling something off, which is what cancel means.

clue.text: Special effects embedding golden palace pet once

indicators.note: embedding something fixes it firmly inside another thing

parts.note: CGI is computer-generated imagery, film special effects
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Film effects show a gilded palace with a pet from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II famously kept corgis at Buckingham Palace, so a corgi was once a palace pet.

clue.text: Pale grey arsenic layer

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
a hen is a layer of eggs

explanation.surface: A grey layer of arsenic coats something.
explanation.walkthrough: Layer suggests a stratum, but it means something that lays, here eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means the colour of ash, a pallid grey, as of a frightened face.

clue.text: Deer full of energy and spirit

indicators.note: something full of another holds it within

parts.note: a hart is a male red deer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lively deer full of energy and vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart in the sense of courage or enthusiasm is the same as spirit.

clue.text: Control the course of one on the ranch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to guide or direct
second meaning: a young castrated bull raised for beef

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second meaning as a playful example: cattle are what you find on a ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to guide a vehicle or course, and the noun names a bullock reared for beef.

clue.text: Ducks circling room in airport buildings

indicators.note: circling something means going all round it, so one piece encloses the rest

parts.note: teal are small freshwater ducks
RM is the abbreviation for room
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ducks fly round a room inside the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' reads as a link before the definition, but it is part of the enclosed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminals are the buildings at an airport where passengers depart and arrive.

clue.text: Hardy doctor around half of us experienced

indicators.note: around places one piece wrapped about another

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is just one of its letters

parts.note: the first of the two letters of us
experienced in the sense of skilled and capable

explanation.surface: A hardy medic has looked after some of us.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy looks like the novelist Thomas Hardy, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something durable is hard-wearing and tough, the same as hardy.

clue.text: Diet ace blended something cool

indicators.note: blended things are mixed together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A slimming champion mixes up a chilled drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea is a chilled drink, served cold with ice, so it is cool refreshment.
